name: Track champion job changes with Gmail bounces, Apollo, AI and Slack alerts

parameters.content:
## Valari: track champion job changes and alert the right rep

**Who it's for:** B2B sales, customer success and GTM teams who want to know when people who used their product move to a new company, without paying for a job-change tool.

### How it works
1. **Every morning** it reads your champions from Google Sheets and scans Gmail for bounces and "no longer with the company" auto-replies. A monthly sweep also checks a third of the list.
2. Each person with a signal is looked up in **Apollo**, within a **monthly credit budget** you set (with a Slack warning at 80%). Recent results are reused instead of paying twice.
3. An **AI agent** decides: confirmed move, **[VERIFY]** or no change, with evidence and a draft opener.
4. Moves are **scored** (role, persona, seniority, account status, ICP fit, recency) and posted to **Slack** with an @mention for the owner, plus their new work email when Apollo has it. Optional: **Hunter** fills in missing emails.
5. **Every other Monday** a digest goes to Slack.
6. A **webhook** sends "call now" alerts when a moved champion opens your email or their new company visits your site.

Nothing is ever sent to a champion automatically. State is kept in n8n Data Tables, created on the first run.

### Set up (about 15 minutes)
1. Make a Google Sheet with a **Champions** tab and a **Customers** tab ([template](https://github.com/sid-sawant-duke/valari/raw/main/sheet/valari-template.xlsx)).
2. Add credentials: Google Sheets, Gmail, Slack, your AI model, and a Header Auth credential for Apollo (name `x-api-key`).
3. Fill in **Config**: sheet ID, Slack channel, Apollo monthly budget, product, ICP, personas, team directory.
4. Put a contact ID in **Test Contact**, run **Test One Person**, then publish the workflow (top right).

### Customize
- **Personas and scoring:** reward the roles you care about (for example UX researchers) instead of only seniority.
- **Any AI model:** swap **Chat Model** for OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama and others.
- **Full version** with a lookup waterfall (Apollo, Clay, People Data Labs), Salesforce, Salesloft and plug-in connectors for any CRM: [GitHub](https://github.com/sid-sawant-duke/valari).

## 1. Triggers and settings
Four ways in: the daily run, a one-person test, the biweekly digest and the "call now" webhook. They all share **Config**.

## 2. Detect
Reads the watchlist, accounts, saved state, lookup cache and credit usage, scans the inbox for bounces and "I've left" auto-replies, and picks who to investigate.

## 3. Look up and investigate
Looks each person up in Apollo (skipping anyone looked up recently, and never past the monthly budget), then the AI agent weighs the evidence and writes a draft opener.

## 4. Score, save and alert
Scores each move, uses the email Apollo found (or optionally asks Hunter), saves the case and posts to Slack.

## Digest
Every other Monday: confirmed moves, open [VERIFY] cases and the funnel.

## "Call now" alerts
Point your sequencing tool (email opened, clicked, replied) and website visitor tool (RB2B, Warmly, Snitcher, Leadfeeder and others) at the webhook. Any JSON with an email or a company domain works.

### Fill in Config first
Sheet ID, Slack channel, Apollo monthly budget, product and ICP descriptions, personas and team directory (Slack member IDs for @mentions).

Set `find_new_emails` to `true` after adding a Hunter credential.

### Apollo
Header Auth credential: name `x-api-key`, value your Apollo API key. Apollo only charges when it finds someone, and phone numbers are never requested.

### Hunter (optional)
Header Auth credential: name `X-API-KEY`, value your API key. Then set `find_new_emails` to `true` in Config.

assignments.name: product_description
assignments.value: REPLACE: describe your product in one or two sentences.

assignments.name: icp_description
assignments.value: REPLACE: describe your ideal customer (company type, size, team).

assignments.name: opener_guidelines
assignments.value: Warm and plain. 2 to 4 sentences, under 70 words. Congratulate them, mention what they did with our product before, offer help getting set up. No hard pitch.

assignments.name: gmail_search_query
assignments.value: newer_than:3d (from:mailer-daemon OR from:postmaster OR subject:("delivery status notification" OR undeliverable OR "undelivered mail" OR "mail delivery failed" OR "returned mail" OR "delivery has failed") OR "no longer with" OR "has left the company" OR "no longer employed" OR "is no longer")

options.systemMessage:
You are the Investigator for Valari, a GTM team's job-change tracker. A champion is someone who used or bought our product at a previous company. Your job is to find out whether this person has moved to a new company, and to say how sure you are, using only the lookup you are given and what your tools return.

## What you get

The person's record, the reason we are checking, and a lookup that has already been run for them (under "Lookup result"). It comes from whichever lookup tool found them first, such as Apollo, Clay or People Data Labs, named in `provider`. Start from that lookup.

## Tools

- `search` (web search, only if it is connected): use it when the lookup found nothing or conflicts with the inbox signal. Good queries: the person's full name plus their likely new company, or full name plus title plus city. At most 2 searches, and never the same query twice.
- `thinking_tool`: a scratchpad to reason through conflicting evidence. Optional.

## How to read the lookup result

- `job_company_name`, `job_company_website`, `job_title`, `job_start_date`: their current primary role.
- `job_last_changed` and `job_last_verified`: when the role data last changed and was last confirmed. Recent dates mean fresher data.
- `experience`: past and present roles. A role with no `end_date` is current. `is_primary: true` marks the main job.
- Some tools (Apollo, Clay) don't give verification dates. When `job_last_verified` is empty, judge freshness from `job_start_date` and the work history.
- A 404, "not found" or "no matching person" result means no match. That is not evidence that they moved. A result whose note starts with "Lookup failed" means the tool errored; say so in the evidence.

## Decide the outcome

- `confirmed`: a reliable source shows a current primary role at a company that is different from their last known company. Fill in `new_company`, `new_company_domain`, `new_title` and `started_new_role` (YYYY-MM if known).
- `verify`: there is a reason to think they left (a bounce, an auto-reply, an ended role) but no reliable source shows the new company yet, or sources conflict, or the only evidence is a single weak web mention.
- `no_change`: the data shows they are still at their last known company and nothing suggests otherwise.

Set `side_role` to true if the only new role is a board seat, advisor, investor, part-time, freelance, volunteer, or "stealth" role. Those are not real moves.

Confidence:
- `high`: a recent, specific source (for example a lookup showing a new role with a start date after the bounce, or a recent `job_last_verified`), or two independent sources that agree.
- `medium`: one decent source.
- `low`: weak, old, or partial evidence.

`icp_fit` for the new company, judged against the ICP description you are given: `strong`, `partial`, `weak`, or `unknown` if you have no basis to judge. Do not search just to judge ICP fit. If the product or ICP description still starts with "REPLACE", it has not been filled in: use `unknown` for ICP fit and keep the opener generic.

## Evidence

Write 1 to 4 short lines, each starting with "- ". Name the source and the date if you have one, for example: "- Apollo: Director of Operations at Acme since 2026-09". Never invent a source, a date, or a URL. If a tool returned nothing useful, say so.

## Draft opener

Only when the outcome is `confirmed`. Write a short first message the rep could send, following the opener guidelines you are given (by default: 2 to 4 sentences, under 70 words, warm and plain). Congratulate them on the new role, mention what they did with our product before (use the relationship notes if there are any), and offer to help them get set up at the new company. No placeholders like [Name], no sign-off name, no em dashes. Leave it empty for any other outcome.

## Rules

- Use only what your tools returned and the facts you were given. Do not guess a new employer from a name match alone. Common names need a matching detail (past company, title, or city) before you trust a result.
- Never contact the person, and never suggest scraping LinkedIn.
- Respond only in the required structured format.
